rows.definition: A top-level `fak` verb classified TierFrontdoor by internal/devindex: the product surface an operator FACES (what `fak help` lists), and the headline heaviness input counted by the frontdoor_verbs meter.
rows.distinction: The product front door - NOT a dev verb (the fak dev tooling tier, TierDev, counted separately in dev_verbs), NOT the `fak dev` namespace (the command that gates the dev tier), NOT devindex (the catalog that ASSIGNS the tier), and NOT TierHidden (internal re-exec seams, never a user verb).

rows.definition: A top-level verb NOT classified frontdoor (TierDev): the `fak dev <verb>` tooling tier - repo-workflow verbs, scorecards, RSI. It stays MEASURED in the dev_verbs meter even after its bare spelling is gated behind `fak dev` (the honesty fence: hidden from the front door, not from the meter).
rows.distinction: The tooling tier that stays on the meter - NOT a frontdoor verb (the product surface, TierFrontdoor, the headline heaviness input), NOT the `fak dev` namespace (one dev verb is an entry; the namespace groups them), and NOT TierHidden (internal seams, never surfaced as a user verb at all).

rows.definition: The CLI namespace that dispatches the dev-tier verbs (resolveDevVerb, cmd/fak/dev.go) and behind which the bare dev spellings are gated - a COMMAND surface that reads devindex to decide what is dev-tier.
rows.distinction: A command namespace - NOT dev-ex (a GitHub developer-experience routing LABEL an issue carries, not a command), NOT devindex (the catalog package it reads to decide tiers), and NOT a dev verb (a single entry, vs the namespace that groups them).

rows.definition: internal/devindex: the CATALOG that classifies every verb's tier (TierFrontdoor / TierDev / TierHidden) from the live dispatch switch - the WITNESSED source the two operator-heaviness meters read to split frontdoor_verbs from dev_verbs.
rows.distinction: The tier catalog - NOT the `fak dev` namespace (the CLI surface that CONSUMES this catalog), NOT dev-ex (a GitHub routing label; same dev root, a catalog package vs an issue tag), and NOT a verb of either tier (it assigns the tier, it is not itself a surfaced verb).
